items.title: Closed, discriminated top-level evidence envelope
items.statement: The schema explicitly closes the top-level object, pins both schema_id and artifact_type, and requires the core artifact, project, run, attempt, routing, projection, retention, and payload fields. This prevents silent top-level field drift and wrong artifact-kind substitution at basic validation time.

items.title: Projection state and creation time are semantically unconstrained
items.statement: created_at_utc is only a nonempty string, while projection_freshness and projection_health accept any string. Invalid timestamps, unknown spellings, contradictory states, and unsupported state transitions therefore validate and cannot be compared reliably by consumers or presented truthfully in a GUI.
items.impact: Consumers can accept malformed time and invented health/freshness states, defeating ordering, alerting, UI truth, and deterministic test oracles.
items.builder_discretion: Define a date-time format and closed state vocabularies with documented legal combinations/transitions, or reference authoritative shared definitions.

items.title: Opaque references lack target and resolution contracts
items.statement: thread_id, node_id, provider_attempt_ref, usage_event_ref, receipt_refs, producer_ref, actor_ref, detail_ref, content_ref, and routing_refs are generic strings without namespaces, target types, URI or identifier formats, referential-integrity expectations, cardinality semantics, or missing-target behavior. Callers and consumers cannot know how to resolve or validate them.
items.impact: The artifact may validate while routing to nonexistent, ambiguous, cross-project, or wrong-kind records; independent consumers can implement incompatible resolution rules.
items.builder_discretion: Bind each reference to a typed identifier or reference schema, define ownership/tenant scope and missing-target behavior, and specify which consumers must dereference each field.

items.title: No concurrency, ordering, or idempotency contract
items.statement: The envelope identifies an artifact and attempt but has no revision, sequence, generation, idempotency key, causal predecessor, optimistic-concurrency token, or uniqueness rule. Concurrent producers can emit clashing or out-of-order evidence with no schema-visible winner or duplicate policy.
items.impact: Retries and concurrent writers can produce duplicates, stale overwrites, or nondeterministic projections even though each artifact validates independently.
items.builder_discretion: Specify uniqueness and immutability rules plus an ordering/idempotency mechanism appropriate to the artifact store.

items.title: Partial-reference and payload failure states are not representable
items.statement: The schema can require routing_refs and a nonempty type_payload, but it cannot state that referenced detail/content/receipts are pending, unavailable, corrupt, partially written, or permanently failed, nor distinguish an intentionally absent optional reference from a failed production step.
items.impact: A superficially valid envelope can conceal incomplete evidence, and consumers have no consistent degrade, retry, or quarantine behavior.
items.builder_discretion: Model completeness and dependency-resolution status, including error reasons and retryability, separately from projection health.

items.title: No supersession, reconstruction, or rollback lineage
items.statement: There is no predecessor, supersedes, derived-from, invalidates, rebuild generation, tombstone, or rollback field. After discovering bad evidence, the model provides no interoperable way to preserve history while identifying a replacement or restored projection.
items.impact: Recovery may require destructive mutation or out-of-band conventions, making replay and audit trails ambiguous.
items.builder_discretion: Define immutable correction/supersession lineage and explicit rebuild or invalidation semantics.

items.title: Producer and actor claims are optional, opaque, and unauthenticated
items.statement: producer_ref and actor_ref are optional arbitrary strings, and the schema has no authority scope, tenant boundary, attestation, signature, digest, or verification status. Any producer able to submit JSON can claim another actor or project and inject evidence unless an unstated external control rejects it.
items.impact: Evidence provenance, authorization, and cross-project isolation cannot be established from the artifact contract.
items.builder_discretion: Require authenticated producer provenance and define authorization and integrity verification outside or within the envelope, including project/run ownership checks.

items.title: Retention label does not define privacy lifecycle
items.statement: retention_class is an arbitrary required string with no classification vocabulary, expiration, legal hold, subject ownership, consent basis, residency, encryption, redaction, deletion receipt, or cascading treatment for detail_ref/content_ref/type_payload.
items.impact: Sensitive runtime evidence can be retained, exposed, or deleted inconsistently, while external content may outlive the envelope or be removed prematurely.
items.builder_discretion: Use a governed retention classification and define expiry, hold, redaction, referenced-content propagation, and verifiable disposal semantics.

items.title: Open, unbounded payload and strings create an untrusted-input sink
items.statement: type_payload requires one property but otherwise permits arbitrary keys, values, nesting, and size. Most strings and arrays also lack maxima, patterns, normalization, or uniqueness. Schema-valid inputs can carry oversized, deeply nested, executable-looking, control-character, or parser-confusing content into downstream renderers and stores.
items.impact: Consumers face denial of service, injection, storage amplification, log corruption, and incompatible interpretation risks despite successful schema validation.
items.builder_discretion: Dispatch type_payload through a closed subtype schema and impose size, depth, count, encoding, and display-sanitization limits at trust boundaries.

items.title: GUI cannot distinguish asserted projection labels from verified truth
items.statement: The envelope exposes projection_freshness and projection_health but no observation time, evaluator, reason, source revision, verification method, confidence, or last-success/last-error data. A GUI can display authoritative-looking green or fresh states that are merely arbitrary producer strings.
items.impact: Operators may act on stale or unverified evidence while the interface appears healthy.
items.builder_discretion: Bind projection state to evaluated-at time, evaluator/revision, reason, and verification provenance; define unknown and stale presentation states.

items.title: Offline, delayed-sync, and conflict states are absent
items.statement: The contract has no local/remote origin, connectivity, sync checkpoint, queued-at, acknowledged-at, conflict, cache completeness, or retry state. Offline-created evidence and network-partitioned projections cannot be distinguished from fully persisted, current evidence.
items.impact: Clients may overstate durability or freshness, lose queued evidence, or resolve reconnect conflicts inconsistently.
items.builder_discretion: Define persistence and synchronization state separately from semantic projection health, including reconnect conflict and retry rules.

items.title: No scale bounds or reference uniqueness
items.statement: receipt_refs and routing_refs have no maxItems or uniqueItems, strings have no maxLength, and type_payload has no maximum properties, byte size, or depth. Duplicate routes and pathological payloads remain valid.
items.impact: A single valid artifact can cause unbounded storage, validation, fan-out, rendering, or dereference work and repeated downstream actions.
items.builder_discretion: Specify bounded sizes/counts/depth and route/reference deduplication, with overflow behavior.

items.title: Accessibility is not directly specified by this storage envelope
items.statement: This line defines a machine-readable artifact data contract rather than an interactive control or rendered presentation. No accessibility behavior can be established or contradicted by the envelope alone; accessibility obligations attach to consuming surfaces. The optional summary remains plain text and does not itself introduce an inaccessible UI primitive.

items.title: Human-readable content has no locale or localization contract
items.statement: summary is an unconstrained string and the envelope has no locale, language, message key, parameters, directionality, or fallback metadata. Producers may persist localized prose without allowing consumers to select, re-render, or correctly format it for another locale.
items.impact: Evidence summaries can be inconsistent, non-localizable, or ambiguous across operators and export contexts.
items.builder_discretion: Clarify whether summary is invariant diagnostic text or localized content; if user-facing, store locale or structured message identifiers and parameters.

items.title: Envelope version and artifact discriminator are explicit
items.statement: The constant schema_id and artifact_type provide deterministic envelope-version and artifact-kind discrimination, which is a sound compatibility seam for dispatching this version.

items.title: Payload compatibility and migration are unspecified
items.statement: Although the envelope is versioned, type_payload has no subtype discriminator, payload schema identifier, payload version, compatibility range, migration provenance, or unknown-subtype handling. Changing payload meaning can silently break consumers without changing the v1 envelope.
items.impact: Two producers can emit schema-valid but mutually incompatible payloads, and old consumers cannot safely reject, preserve, or migrate new variants.
items.builder_discretion: Add a closed payload discriminator/version and define forward/backward compatibility plus lossless unknown-payload preservation or rejection rules.

items.title: Core run correlation and creation metadata are required
items.statement: project_id, run_id, attempt_id, and created_at_utc are mandatory and nonempty, establishing a minimum correlation surface for operational lookup even though their formats and integrity remain underspecified.

items.title: Operational diagnostics and support lineage are too thin
items.statement: The envelope lacks trace/span or correlation identifiers, ingestion time, producer version, validation outcome, error code/reason, last transition time, integrity digest, and support-safe diagnostic references. Optional producer_ref and summary cannot provide dependable observability.
items.impact: Operators cannot reliably trace evidence production, distinguish producer from ingestion delay, verify payload integrity, or diagnose failed projections.
items.builder_discretion: Define the minimal trace, producer-version, transition, integrity, and diagnostic fields needed for operational support.

items.title: Retention-driven destruction lacks hold, cascade, and proof semantics
items.statement: The required retention_class implies eventual lifecycle action, but the contract does not define who may delete evidence, how legal holds override expiry, whether referenced content is cascaded, how shared targets are protected, or how tombstones and deletion receipts preserve auditability.
items.impact: Cleanup can destroy required evidence or leave sensitive referenced content behind, with no verifiable record of the action.
items.builder_discretion: Specify authorized deletion, hold precedence, reference-aware cascade rules, and durable deletion/tombstone receipts.

items.title: Cross-document seams are syntactically present but not contractually bound
items.statement: The many *_ref fields and routing_refs expose seams to other records, yet none identifies a target schema, owner, canonical key space, required project/run consistency, resolution transaction, or behavior when the target evolves or is absent.
items.impact: Schema-valid documents can violate neighboring contracts and produce dangling or cross-context links that are only discovered at runtime.
items.builder_discretion: Reference shared typed-ref definitions and assert cross-record invariants in an executable integration validator.

items.title: Structural rejection is testable but semantic correctness is not
items.statement: Tests can falsify missing required fields, extra top-level properties, wrong constants, empty identifiers, empty routing_refs, and empty type_payload. They cannot falsify malformed time, invented state labels, invalid reference targets, inconsistent ownership, unsupported payload variants, or impossible cross-field combinations because the schema accepts them.
items.impact: A green schema-validation suite can create false assurance while core behavioral invariants remain untested and unenforced.
items.builder_discretion: Add schema constraints for local semantics and executable integration/property tests for reference, authorization, lifecycle, and cross-field invariants.

items.title: Envelope closure and payload openness create an ungoverned extension channel
items.statement: The top level is closed while type_payload is effectively open. Future producers are therefore likely to tunnel new envelope-level semantics into arbitrary payload keys, but the line does not reveal whether an external registry, subtype dispatcher, or preservation policy governs those keys. This unknown could amplify compatibility, authority, privacy, and UI-truth failures.
items.impact: Undocumented extensions may become de facto contracts that validators cannot distinguish from accidental or hostile content.
items.builder_discretion: Establish and test a governed extension/subtype mechanism, including ownership, namespacing, versioning, and unknown-field handling.

dimension_assessments.summary: Reference-bearing fields do not name consumers or define resolution and missing-target contracts.
Timestamp and projection-state strings allow malformed and impossible semantic states.
No ordering, revision, uniqueness, or idempotency rules address concurrent production and retry races.
Incomplete or failed referenced content cannot be distinguished from intentional absence.
No supersession, invalidation, rebuild, or rollback lineage exists.
Actor and producer claims lack required authenticated provenance, scope, and integrity binding.
An arbitrary retention label does not govern classification, expiry, holds, redaction, or referenced-content lifecycle.
Open payloads and unbounded strings, arrays, and nesting form an unsafe input surface.
Projection labels lack verification provenance and can be rendered as authoritative truth.
Persistence, synchronization, queued, conflict, and reconnect states are absent.
No maxima, depth limits, or reference uniqueness bound validation and fan-out cost.
The reviewed line is a machine-readable storage envelope and specifies no interactive or rendered accessibility behavior; consuming surfaces retain that obligation.
Human-readable summary text has no locale, message-key, parameter, directionality, or fallback semantics.
Envelope discrimination is explicit, but payload versioning, compatibility, unknown variants, and migration are not.
Required run correlation is useful, but trace, producer version, transition, integrity, and diagnostics are absent.
Retention-driven deletion lacks authorization, hold precedence, reference-aware cascade, tombstone, and proof semantics.
Generic references are not bound to target schemas, owners, key spaces, or cross-record invariants.
Structural negatives are testable, but most semantic invariants remain unfalsifiable under this schema.
The line does not reveal whether an external payload registry governs the open extension channel created by a closed envelope and arbitrary type_payload.
